sources.entry: Black Candy - Music streaming server. MIT Docker/Ruby

summary.one_liner: Black Candy is a self-hosted music streaming server, run as a Docker image, that serves your own music library through a web interface and mobile apps.
summary.what_it_does: Black Candy runs as a personal music streaming server that you host yourself. The README describes a Docker image that serves on port 80 and is configured through environment variables such as MEDIA_PATH for the music directory. It uses SQLite by default and can switch to PostgreSQL via DB_ADAPTER and related URL variables. Data such as sessions and databases persists in /rails/storage, and a SECRET_KEY_BASE value can be set for stable sessions. Optional Discogs API tokens can be added in the settings page to fetch artist and album images. The README also mentions mobile apps in app stores and an Android APK on GitHub Releases.
use_cases: stream my own music library from a home server
host a personal music center in a browser
run a self-hosted Spotify-like music server
serve a media folder over the web to my devices
fetch artist and album art for a local music collection
notable: Ships as a Docker image with a docker-compose example and SQLite as the default database
Supports PostgreSQL as an alternative database through environment variables
Media library is set by mounting a host folder and setting MEDIA_PATH, or in the settings page
Optional Discogs integration for artist and album images
Includes a demo mode (DEMO_MODE) that restricts admin privileges and profile changes
caveats: The README warns that upgrades may include breaking changes and points to a separate upgrade guide
The edge version tracks the master branch and the README advises ordinary users against it because of possible data loss
Without SECRET_KEY_BASE set, sessions are invalidated on every container restart
keywords: listen to my music from home
